title: ENSEMBLE-REF: can a stronger reference be built from the eval set's own strongest models? (free check, zero calls)
question: Majority vote of the top-6 contestants' static answers as a reference, and the leave-two-out variant a real match would actually get (its two contestants excluded): does it beat grok-reasoning's 0.860 pool / 0.743 hard-stratum (confidence < 100) accuracy?

plain_description.what: The answers of the 6 strongest models in the set were combined by majority vote to build a reference answer for the judge. The result was compared with the single reasoning-model reference, overall and on hard questions. No calls were made.
plain_description.why: It asks whether a better reference for the judge can be built from the models being evaluated.
plain_description.information: A higher accuracy would give a cheap, stronger reference. The same accuracy would mean a better reference must come from outside the set. Result: done. It is not stronger: 0.875 overall and 0.772 on hard questions, the same ceiling as the single reference. The hard questions are hard for every model in the set. Older p2dca data family: history, not evidence.
